root.name: Slav Defense: Süchting Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 Qb6

overview: Black plays 4...Qb6 attacking d4 and b2, so White has to defend with Qd2 or Na4 or take a pawn with Nxd5. The early queen move breaks the usual Slav pattern and tries to take White out of theory. White normally gets a modest edge from space and development.

white_ideas.idea: Defend d4 and b2 with Na4 or Qd2 and keep the centre
Use the extra development against the queen

black_ideas.idea: Hit b2 and d4 with the queen

typical_structures.structure: Slav structure with c6 and d5 against c4 and d4

character.notes: Not well known to me; reasoned from the move order.

gambit.notes: Pawns can be defended without material changing hands.

soundness.notes: White is a little better but the line is not refuted.

structure.notes: Slav centre with the c- and d-pawns and a partly open c-file.

approach.notes: A sideline of the Slav that strong players play now and then.

character.reason: The queen sortie adds tactics but White can defend simply.

soundness.reason: Black is not at clear risk.

structure.reason: Slav centre with a partly open c-file.

approach.reason: Played by strong players from time to time.

plans.reason: The queen comes to b6 early.
